Self-Starting
Develop a plan you can execute without waiting for things to happen.
Be open to change and adapt your plan from time to time.
Look at how long it takes other people to complete similar tasks as an indicator of how
long your own plan might take.

Future-oriented
Set milestones - it is better to have rough plans than no plans.
Look at your plan from an outsider's perspective: Is there anything that could go
wrong in the future? Prepare now!
What opportunities might come your way in achieving your goal? Plan now!
Overcoming obstacles :
Make at least one plan B per obstacle in case your plan A does not work.
Plans often don't work out. It’s better to adapt your plan rather than abandon your
goal.

EXERCISE: Creating a Plan From a Goal
Case study : Caroline and the miniature T-Shirts
Caroline has a cutting and sewing workshop. She specialises in Work Wear,
customised T-Shirts, and Tracksuits, and has three permanent employees (Garment
workers). Her creations are well made, of high quality and therefore durable.
Caroline has been keeping her own business accounts since starting her business,
so she knows exactly how much money she makes in sales each month, what her
expenses amount to, and important information about her customers (how many,
who came and what they purchased).
WS
31
On average, Caroline has 25 clients per month. She’s decided to put more energy into
increasing her customer base, and set herself the goal of growing the number of
customers from 25 to 35 per month over the next 4 months by using a creative way to
advertise her products.
Instead of using paper business cards like everyone else, Caroline wants to print her
contact details on miniature T-shirts. She sets herself the following goal:
"I want to increase the number of customers from 25 to 35 per month over the next 4
months by distributing miniature T-shirts as business cards.
What you need to know about Caroline is that her workshop is located outside the city
and she has limited money available.

FRESE GROUP, LEUPHANA UNIVERSITY OF LÜNEBURG 1
WS 1
EXERCISE
CASE STUDY:
ANNIE
Identify proactive behaviour
and its consequences.
Hello, I am Annie. I produce and sell herbs from my region. Before that, I worked for
four years in a food laboratory. To learn how to run a business, I regularly watch
videos on the internet about accounting and management. My business has grown
steadily over the past few years. I recently set myself the goal of doubling my
turnover within a year. To get higher prices for my products, I tried to contact a large
supermarket in Juba. As no one responded to my request for contact, I asked a
friend, who works for the supermarket chain, to bring a sample of my products to
his manager and refer to my offer. In this way, I was able to attract the attention of
the management and started a collaboration with the supermarket.
In order to be able to deliver his products to the supermarkets in Juba, I collaborate
with a local farmer, who often travels to the city for his business. I am also working
to ensure that my products meet the criteria to be certified "organic". I think that
organic products will be more and more in demand in the years to come.
WHAT IS ANNIE'S ACTIVE BEHAVIOUR?
WHAT ARE THE CONSEQUENCES OF THIS
BEHAVIOUR?
FRESE GROUP, LEUPHANA UNIVERSITY OF LÜNEBURG 2
WS 2
EXERCISE
CASE STUDY :
PAULINE
Identify reactive behaviour and
its consequences.
Hello, my name is Pauline. I learned from my parents about the production and
marketing of herbs. When they got older, I took over their business. I basically
stuck to my parents' business routine, because so far it has worked well, therefore,
I’ve never really looked for new ways to increase production or improve marketing.
However, one of my main problems is packaging and selling my herbs. As the
road is in a very bad condition, it takes me a long time to get to the capital to buy
the packaging I need. As a result, I usually avoid travelling and often run out of
boxes and bags for my products. For the same reason, I can’t easily participate in
the big trade markets where my competitors exhibit their products and look for
new business partners. Not selling fast enough also means that I lack space to
store my products. Despite all this, I can’t think of anything I can do. I just hope
that one day there will be a new road.
WHAT IS PAULINE'S REACTIVE BEHAVIOUR?
WHAT ARE THE CONSEQUENCES OF THIS
BEHAVIOUR?
